headline: High-risk default filesystem and shell overlap: Open Interpreter can read/write and execute on the same local machine while mem0 may ingest or persist shared content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter can read the filesystem, clipboard, and stdin/stdout, so mem0 content placed in shared files or copied text can be treated as instructions. mem0 is a knowledge-management agent with no documented isolation or provenance controls here. The pathway exists in default local workflows, though it is not a shared MCP channel.
conditions: IF mem0 outputs are copied into Open Interpreter prompts or files
IF Open Interpreter ingests shared files as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep mem0 and Open Interpreter on separate workspaces
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Prefix mem0 outputs with explicit untrusted-data markers
Review any file before Open Interpreter reads it
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter can read the entire user filesystem and has broad network egress, so any mem0-managed notes or secrets on disk can be exposed externally. mem0 touches memory content, and no profile field shows encryption, access control, or redaction. This is a default dangerous path with potentially irreversible exfiltration.
conditions: IF mem0 stores sensitive notes on the local filesystem
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to read those files and call external model providers
mitigations: Store mem0 data in a separate encrypted volume
Restrict Open Interpreter to a narrow directory
Disable network egress for Open Interpreter during mem0 access
Remove secrets from shared folders before running either agent
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem sandboxing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter has write_filesystem and modify_git_state, while mem0 is a knowledge-management system that may also persist state through files or integrations. The pair shares the filesystem as the concurrency boundary, and no locking or coordination primitive is documented. Concurrent writes can corrupt shared state or git history.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory
IF mem0 state is stored in files that Open Interpreter edits or commits
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Avoid git operations on shared worktrees
Use file backups before edits
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can act on filesystem and shell outputs, so if mem0-produced content is treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into commands or commits. mem0 is a memory layer, not a verifier, and no verification step is documented between them. The blast radius is multiple work products rather than immediate irreversible harm.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter uses mem0 output as facts or instructions
IF the output is forwarded into shell commands or git commits without review
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Treat mem0 output as untrusted input
Add a verification step against source documents
Limit Open Interpreter to read-only mode for mem0-derived tasks
requires-engineering: implement output validation

E_compliance.rationale: mem0 is a memory system and Open Interpreter can access anything reachable on the local machine, so residency and retention obligations can be violated if regulated data is stored locally and then processed by external model providers. Only Open Interpreter is cited because the compliance risk is driven by its documented local-machine access and outbound model-provider calls; mem0 has no specific residency controls shown.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in mem0 on the local machine
IF Open Interpreter sends that data to configured external model providers
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from mem0
Use local-only model providers
Delete sensitive files before processing
Review retention settings for any provider
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
